summary: Master social protection for refugees and stateless persons. Learn to design inclusive safety nets, cash-based interventions, and digital identity systems.
lede: Social protection for refugees and stateless persons connects essential services, income security, and legal rights across the displacement cycle. This course shows how to integrate humanitarian assistance into social safety nets while strengthening resilience and self-reliance. You will develop practical skills in legal eligibility analysis, vulnerability profiling, digital payment management, cross-sector coordination, and impact reporting. You will also apply protection-sensitive approaches to social registries, cash assistance, vulnerability dashboards, labor market pathways, and shock-responsive systems while addressing documentation barriers and data privacy concerns.
audienceIntro: This intermediate-level program is designed for professionals who manage or influence the delivery of services to displaced and stateless populations within humanitarian and development contexts.
audience: NGO Advocacy Leads focused on labor market
Development Bank Analysts focused on forced displacement
modules: International Legal Frameworks for Displaced Persons
Social Protection Floors and Displaced Populations
Labor Market Inclusion and Economic Self-Reliance
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 3 years of experience in humanitarian assistance, social policy, or refugee protection. Familiarity with the 1951 Refugee Convention and basic social assistance concepts is recommended. No advanced technical skills are required, though a basic understanding of data management is beneficial.
